thread:
Maria Zhou: heads up — during the quarterly audit I found ~12 accounts that still had KMS key access after SCIM deprovision. :grimacing:
Maria Zhou: traced it to the provisioner logs, looks like a concurrent group update overwrote the `kms_tags` blob with an empty payload during a group rename race.
Ajay Patel: can you paste the log snippet? timeline + request ids?
Maria Zhou: sure — here's the relevant tail from staging (redacted):
```
2025-09-14T16:22:11Z request_id=rc-9f4a scim: PATCH /Groups/123
2025-09-14T16:22:11Z provisioner: fetch-group current={members:[u1,u2],tags:{env:prod,kms:team-a}}
2025-09-14T16:22:11Z provisioner: apply-update with body={members:[u2],tags:{}}  <-- unexpected empty tags
2025-09-14T16:22:11Z provisioner: write-iam-policy ok
2025-09-14T16:22:11Z async-kms: sync-tags request_id=rc-9f4a payload={}  <-- lost tags
2025-09-14T16:22:12Z scim: PATCH /Groups/123 request_id=rc-9f4b rename-group -> members & tags set correctly
```
Maria Zhou: looks like two SCIM PATCHes overlapped; the first came from a scripted deprovision removing a user and used a minimal body (omitting tags), and the code path does a blind write to the group metadata instead of merge/etag check.
Leo Kim: ugh. So when the tags disappear, KMS key policies lose the team tag and fallback IAM grants stay around?
Samir Gomez: yep — key policy reconciliation relies on `kms:tags` existing. If tags are removed we don't trigger revocation because reconciliation sees key still bound to principal in the legacy allow list.
Elaine Park: this could affect Private customers if they do automated group renames/deprovisions. We should run a detection query for keys with stale team tags.
Ajay Patel: action plan? I'll reproduce in staging and add an e2e test for concurrent SCIM ops. Can someone own a quick fix?
Samir Gomez: hotfix options: (1) apply optimistic locking with etag on group metadata and reject blind writes, (2) always treat missing tags as noop instead of erase, or (3) merge server-side: fetch, merge, CAS write. I prefer (3) for safety.
Maria Zhou: +1 on merge CAS. Also we should special-case `tags` to never be cleared by an absent field in the SCIM body.
Ajay Patel: I'll put up a small PR for the merge behavior in the provisioner runtime (staging-only initially). Will add a golden test for simultaneous PATCHes.
Elaine Park: detection SQL to find possibly affected keys (run against audit-index):
```
SELECT key_id, last_tag_state, last_sync_ts
FROM kms_key_audit
WHERE last_tag_state NOT LIKE '%team:%' AND last_sync_ts BETWEEN now()-interval '30 days' AND now();
```
Elaine Park: we should run that and triage top-10 by last_sync_ts.
Maria Zhou: repro steps for Ajay: 1) create group G with tags {team:alpha,kms:team-a} 2) in parallel: (A) PATCH members remove user X with body {members:[...]} (B) PATCH rename group with body {displayName:"G-renamed", members:[...], tags:{team:alpha,kms:team-a}} — ensure A omits tags field.
Ajay Patel: got it. I'll run 1000 parallel trials with small delay jitter to increase race probability.
Samir Gomez: we should also add a background reconciliation job to detect and repair missing tags on keys: if key references team in policy but tag missing, reapply tag or revoke grants depending on policy.
Maria Zhou: agreed. Also create an incident note and send a short advisory to support about possible stale access for deprovisioned users in last 30 days. Keep it informational for now.
provisioner-bot: alert: SCIM PATCH concurrency anomaly detected for /Groups/123 at 2025-09-14T16:22:11Z — anomaly_score=0.84
Ajay Patel: assigning tasks — Ajay: repro + test (staging), Samir: reconcile job spec + runtime CAS change, Maria: audit + support advisory, Elaine: run detection query and surface top hits to security ops. ETA: 48h?
Samir Gomez: 48h for spec + hotfix branch.
Maria Zhou: thanks all. I'll draft the support advisory and attach the log snippets. Please post PR links here when ready. :thumbsup:
Ajay Patel: will follow up in this thread with staging results and PR link.
